60-Minute Dal Makhani

Prep time: 10-15 minutes (excluding soaking time)
Cooking time: 1 hour 
Serves: 4-5 people

Ingredients:
Boiled dal
WHOLE URAD DAL | साबुत उरद दाल 1 CUP
WATER | पानी AS REQUIRED 
GARLIC | लहसुन 5 CLOVES
WATER | पानी 1 INCH ABOVE THE DAL
SALT | नमक 1 TSP
KASHMIRI RED CHILLI POWDER | कश्मीरी लाल मिर्च पाउडर 1 TSP
Tempering & final cooking
GHEE | घी 2-3 TBSP
GINGER GARLIC PASTE | अदरक लहसुन की पेस्ट 2 TBSP
KASHMIRI RED CHILLI POWDER | कश्मीरी लाल मिर्च पाउडर 2 TBSP
GARAM MASALA | गरम मसाला 1/4 TSP
TOMATO PUREE | टमाटर की प्यूरी OF 5 TOMATOES 
SALT A PINCH | नमक A PINCH
HOT WATER AS REQUIRED | गरम पानी AS REQUIRED 
FRESH CREAM | फ्रेश क्रीम 2-3 TBSP
WHITE BUTTER | सफेद मक्खन 2-3 TBSP
ROASTED KASURI METHI POWDER | भुनी हुई कसूरी मेथी का पाउडर A LARGE PINCH 
GARAM MASALA A LARGE PINCH | गरम मसाला A LARGE PINCH 
Method:
Add all the dal into a large bowl, add water & wash it by rubbing them in between your palms 3-4 times until the water added turns clear, then let the dal soak for 10-12 hours.
Once soaked wash the dal again similarly until the added water turns clear, discard that water & add the dal into the cooker.
Add garlic, water & kashmiri red chilli powder & pressure cook the dal over high flame for 4 whistles, then switch off the flame & let the cooker depressurize naturally.
Further mash the dal lightly using a potato masher, don’t mash it too much to make a paste, set it aside until you make the tempering.
Set stock pot on high flame & add ghee and let it get hot.
Further add the ginger garlic paste, stir & cook over medium flame for 2 minutes.
Lower the flame & add kashmiri red chilli powder & garam masala, stir well & then add the tomato puree & salt, stir well & cook over high flame until the oil separates & the tomato puree turns crumbly.
Then add the cooked dal, mix well with the tempering & add hot water as required, the dal should become, bring the dal toh a gentle simmer and cook it briefly.
Once the dal has thickened after simmering for, add fresh cream, white butter, roasted kasuri methi powder, garam masala, stir well then taste for salt & adjust accordingly.
Your delicious dal makhani is ready, serve it along with laccha paratha & rice.

Fried rice

Ingredients 

4 cups cooked basmati rice. ( cooked with cumin seeds )
4 tablespoons oil
1 teaspoon of each minced ginger, garlic & green chilies 
1/2 cup finely chopped green beans
1/2 cup finely chopped carrots 
1/2 cup minced onions
1/2 cup chopped mushrooms 
1/2 cup chopped cabbage 
4 eggs beaten with salt
1 tablespoon palm candy ( Rock candy or white sugar can be used )
2 tablespoons chopped green onions and cilantro 

Method

Keep all the ingredients ready , which is the most important tip to making fried rice.

Cook the rice, spread it on a tray and cook for 20 minutes 

Heat oil in a wok. The wok has to be really hot. Add the minced ginger, garlic and chillies. Toss for 3 secs.

Add the red pepper flakes. Mix and immediately add the green beans. Sauté for a 20 secs, add the carrots and toss on high heat for 10 secs. 

Move the veggies to a corner, add oil and toss the onions for 10 secs. Now add the mushrooms and cook for another 20 secs. Add the cabbage , salt and saute for 5secs. 

Make space in the center, add oil, and mix in the eggs . Scramble the eggs and mix it with the veggies. Remove and keep aside.

Heat oil, add the palm candy and let it caramelize. This gives the color to the fried rice, without using soy sauce.

Now add the rice , Mix and add the veggies and eggs. Keep stirring continuously for 1 minute, till everything comes together. 

Add the cilantro and green onions.

Chettinad Mushroom Masala

Chettinad is a region in the Pudukottai district in Tamilnadu, India. Chettinad cuisine is known for its exquisite blend of spices and masala. 

Ingredients 

Spice blend:
1/2- 1 teaspoon whole black pepper 
1 teaspoon cumin seeds
1 teaspoon fennel seeds
A small piece stone flower 
1 teaspoon coriander seeds
4 cloves
3 cardamoms
A small piece of cinnamon 
1-2 red chilies according to taste 
1 tablespoon desiccated coconut 
1/2 teaspoon poppy seeds

Dry roast all the above in a kadai and powder. 

2 tablespoons sesame oil
1/2 teaspoon mustard seeds 
8 big mushrooms chopped into chunks 
1/2 a cup chopped red onion
2 green chilies chopped ( can reduce according to heat)
2 cloves garlic chopped ( optional, I have not used it in the recipe)
1 medium tomato chopped 
1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder 
2 teaspoons spice blend
2 sprigs curry leaves 
2 tablespoons chopped cilantro 
Salt to taste

1. Dry fry the spices, Powder them and keep aside.
2. Heat a kadai and add oil. When hot add the mustard seeds and let it sizzle.
3. Now add the onions and fry till soft. Add the finely minced green chilies.
4. Add the tomatoes and fry till soft.
5. Add the turmeric powder, mix well and add the chopped mushrooms.
6. Add the required amount of spices blend and saute until it is mixed well.
7. Once the mushrooms are fried we’ll add salt.
8.Add the curry leaves, cilantro and mix well. 
9.Serve with rice, roti or bread. 
Enjoy!

Eggplant Dip | Baingan Bhartha 
This recipe can be used as a dip or can be served with rotis.

Ingredients 
1 big globe eggplant cut into two
1 medium red onion
1 head garlic
2 vine ripe tomatoes 
3-4 green chilies 
3 tablespoons oil1 teaspoon cumin seeds
1 teaspoon mustard seeds
1/2 teaspoon black pepper
1/2 - 1 teaspoon chili powder
1/2 a teaspoon turmeric powder 
1/2 teaspoon coriander powder 
1 tablespoons chopped curry leaves 
2 tablespoons chopped cilantro
Salt to taste

Method 
1.Cut the eggplant into half . Remove the outer skins of the onion and garlic. 
2. Sprinkle salt over the eggplant. Smear 2 tablespoons oil over the veggies . 
3. Roast in an oven at 400°F for 40 minutes or over an open fire till charred on the outside ( If you are roasting over the fire keep the eggplant whole and prick holes ) .
4. Once roasted peel the skins of the veggies and chop finely.
5. Toast the cumin seeds and pepper till you get a nice aroma. Now powder this and keep aside.
6. Heat a pot, add 1 tablespoon oil and add mustard seeds. Once it starts to sizzle, add the spices,  salt and immediately add the chopped veggies. Do not let the spices too long, it tends to burn and become bitter. 
7. Add the powdered spice, curry leaves and cilantro and mix well. Serve this as a dip for chips or for rotis .

Dried fenugreek leaves known as Kasoori methi is used in this recipe
Ingredients 

3 cups all purpose flour 
1 teaspoon whole black pepper 
1 teaspoon cumin seeds 
1 teaspoon ajwain ( carom ) seeds 
1 teaspoon chili 
1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder 
2 tablespoons Methi ( dried fenugreek / Kasoori Methi ) leaves 
1 tablespoon butter 
Salt to taste
Oil for frying 

Method

Crush pepper, cumin, ajwain, chili powder, turmeric powder,Methi ( dried fenugreek) levesand salt to a coarse powder. 

Sieve the flour. Add the crushed powder. Add the butter and mix thoroughly. 

Add water and knead into a soft dough. Add 1 tablespoon oil and knead again.

Divide the dough into equal parts. Roll the dough into 1/8th thickness using a pasta roller or by using a rolling pin. Dust with flour to avoid sticking.

Cut into diamond shape pieces according to the size you prefer. 

Deep fry till slightly brown and crisp.

Blanch spinach for 30 seconds, strain cool and chop roughly.
Toast 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 1 red chili and 1/4 tsp pepper ( optional ) till slightly brown and pound in a mortar and pestle.
Heat a pan, add  1 tablespoon oil , add 1/2 cup chopped onions and saute for a minute.
Add the blanched spinach and stir well. Next add the lentils and stir fry for 2 mins.
Add salt, spice powder and 1/4 cup grated coconut and stir fry for 2 minutes.
Enjoy!

Green Papaya Salad

2 cups julienned green papaya ( unripe )
1 tablespoon sesame oil 
2 red chilies broken into pieces 
1/2 tsp cumin seeds 
1 tsp minced garlic 
1/2 tsp turmeric powder 
1 tablespoon tamarind paste 
1 tablespoon palm sugar or brown sugar 
4 tablespoons crushed toasted peanuts 
1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds 
Thai basil leaves 
Lemon juice 
Salt to taste 

Cut the papaya into half. Peel the skin and julienne. 
Heat oil in a pan. When you see smoke, add the cumin seeds and red chilies. Toss till the chilies are dark.
Add the minced garlic. Toss and add the turmeric powder, tamarind paste, palm sugar and salt to taste. Give it one good mix.
Now add the papaya and toss on high heat for just 2 minutes. You should not cook it too much, otherwise it will lose the texture.
Now add the toasted peanuts,sesame seeds and basil leaves. Mix and switch off the heat.
Add lemon juice and mix well. 

Papaya salad is ready, Enjoy!

Kanji
A Refreshing Indian Probiotic Drink
A healthy probiotic drink called Kanji. It’s not just a tasty treat, but also a fantastic way to promote gut health. 

Ingredients
To make Kanji, you’ll need the following ingredients:
1 lb ( 250 gms ) of purple carrots, peeled and julienned
8 oz ( 200 gms ) of red carrots, peeled and julienned
1 lb ( 250 gms ) of beets, peeled and julienned
2 tablespoons of split mustard seeds
1- 11/2 teaspoons of red chili powder
1 teaspoon of turmeric powder
2 teaspoon salt ( I used sea salt )
2 ltrs boiled water
Optional ( 1/8 tsp asafoetida and 1/2 teaspoon black salt )

Preparation
First, wash and peel the black carrots and beets , then cut them into thin julienne strips. The purple carrots and beets give Kanji its distinctive color and flavor.
Bring 2 liters  of water to a boil. Once it’s boiling, switch off and let it cool for a few minutes till warm.
In a glass jar, add the carrots beets, split mustard seeds, turmeric powder, chili powder, salt and optionally hing ( asafoetida ) and black salt.
Add the water and combine well. The spice mix will give our Kanji that unique and flavorful kick.

Now, for the magic touch – fermentation! . 
Seal the container and let it sit in a warm, dark place for about 3-4 days. During this time, the natural fermentation process will take place, creating that bubbly and tangy flavor we love in probiotic drinks. Give it a stir everyday, and check for tanginess .
(After 3-4 days) Our Kanji is ready! Open the container and give it a good stir. You’ll notice the vibrant color and the wonderful aroma. Strain the Kanji to remove the carrot, beet pieces and mustard seeds. This can be eaten as pickles.
Serve it chilled. Cheers to good health with this homemade Kanji!

Milagu vadai / Pepper crispy thins

Ingredients 

1cup Urad dhal
1 teaspoon rice
1 tablespoon crushed pepper 
1 tablespoons crushed cumin seeds
2 tablespoons chopped curry leaves 
A pinch hing ( asafoedita)
Salt to taste
Oil for frying

Method 

Soak Urad dhal and rice for 1 1/2 hours 
Drain and pulse it a few times adding salt and hing. The texture has to be coarse. Do not add water.
Add the pepper, cumin seeds and curry leaves and mix well. 
Heat oil for frying. 
Dip your fingers in water and make a small ball and pat on a wet cloth till it is thin. Make a hole in the center. 
Lift it from the cloth and add to the hot oil and fry till golden brown.

Blueberry Sausage Pancake Casserole

INGREDIENTS
4 cups pancake mix
3 cups water 
1 lb breakfast sausage, browned 
1 1/2 cups fresh blueberries 
1/3 cup maple syrup

INSTRUCTIONS 
First, cook 1 lb of breakfast sausage. Drain the grease well. 

In a large bowl mix together 4 cups of Pancake Mix with water following the directions on the box. Add the browned sausage, blueberries, and maple syrup. I like to keep a little bit of the sausage and blueberries separate to add to the top the breakfast casserole, but that is optional. Stir well. 

Spray a 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray. Add the pancake mixture to the baking dish. Top with the reserved sausage and blueberries. Bake at 375 degrees F for about 40-45 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean from the center of the pancake casserole. 

Top a piece with more maple syrup and enjoy!

Maggi noodles are available in various flavors in India, categorized by base ingredients like classic masala and atta, healthier options like oats and nutri-licious, and specialty ranges such as Hot Heads and Korean BBQ. Some of the common types include Masala, Chicken, and Oats noodles, while specialty variants cater to diverse tastes with flavors like Peri Peri, Cheesy, and Korean BBQ. 

Classic and popular

2-Minute Noodles (Masala): The original and most popular flavor.Chicken Noodles: The only non-vegetarian variant in the popular 2-Minute line.Special Masala: A richer and more flavorful masala version.Veggie Masala Noodles: Includes added vegetables for extra taste and texture. 

Healthier options

Atta Noodles: Made with whole wheat atta, offering a healthier alternative.Nutri-licious: A range of products that includes Atta Masala and Oats Masala variants to provide more nutritional value.Oats Noodles: Another healthy option that uses oats as a base ingredient. 

Specialty and premium

Hot Heads: A range of spicy noodles, such as the Hot Heads Peri Peri.Korean BBQ: Offers a unique flavor profile inspired by Korean cuisine, with both veg and chicken versions.No Onion No Garlic: A specific variant catering to those who avoid onion and garlic. 

Regional flavors

Masalas of India: A range launched to capture regional tastes, with flavors like Super Chennai Masala, Bengali Jhaal Masala, and Mumbai Masala. 

Other variations

Cuppa Noodles: Instant noodles that are served in a cup, ready to eat after adding hot water.Cheesy Maggi: A popular variation where cheese is added to the noodles for a creamy and rich taste.Corn Cheese Maggi: Combines the sweetness of corn with the richness of cheese for a unique flavor.

Elvia Cabrera I second all these suggestions. I am a 4-H Positive Youth Development Extension Educator for Purdue University. Despite popular belief, children do not have to live in a rural area to be involved in 4-H. We offer Jr. Master Gardener programs and gardening projects (hobbies) that kids ages 9-19 can learn about independently and through caring adult mentors. You can also purchase the gardening workbooks on the National 4-H website. Every county in the nation has a 4-H program located at their local County Extension Office. The program offers scholarships, camps, and opportunities to visit the land grant university for career summer camps in most states. Horticulture, botany, plant sciences and urban agriculture degrees would be helpful. Volunteering and shadowing people in the field as well.

4-H teaches more than just gardening. Your child will learn valuable life skills to apply to real-world applications like generosity, responsibility, character, empathy, citizenship, leadership and much more.

Here are some at home activities for gardening: https://4-h.org/about/blog/4-h-at-home-gardening-plant-science/
